title: Hopps: Leveraging Sparsity to Accelerate Automata Processing
problem: Automata processing (AP) workloads execute many finite state machines (FSMs) in parallel over streaming symbol data, but existing AP accelerators suffer poor utilization because most FSMs are inactive (in a non-matching state) for any given input symbol. The irregular, state-dependent activation pattern makes it hard to exploit spatial parallelism efficiently.
method: Hopps exploits the observation that only a sparse subset of FSMs transition on each input symbol. It uses a sparsity-aware representation that tracks only active states across all FSMs and a compressed activation bitmap to skip idle FSMs entirely during each symbol step. The architecture couples this with a tiled SRAM storage layout so that state-transition tables for active FSMs are fetched in bursts, reducing off-chip memory traffic proportional to the active-FSM fraction.

title: SeIM: In-Memory Acceleration for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
problem: ANNS workloads bottleneck on memory bandwidth (extensive random access) and sorting (cross-memory-unit data dependencies), limiting throughput in CPU/GPU/ASIC-based systems and making them inefficient for RAG-based LLM inference.
method: Hierarchical in-memory architecture that offloads memory-bound parallel ANNS operations (vector loading, distance computation) to the memory bank level with minimal DRAM modifications, and places compute-bound sorting at the memory controller level with adaptive transmission filtering to reduce cross-unit data transfers during merge operations.

title: Generalizing Reuse Patterns for Efficient DNN on Microcontrollers
problem: DNN inference on microcontrollers is limited by their restricted compute and memory, and existing computation reuse techniques that exploit redundancy in input/activation data are constrained by a narrow definition of reuse patterns, leaving a large portion of potential reuse unexploited.
method: The work introduces generalized reuse, which frames computation reuse in terms of row and column reordering of a matrix view of DNN input or activation maps. By recognizing that different reorderings expose different reuse patterns, the approach dramatically expands the explorable reuse space beyond what prior narrow pattern definitions allow. Two analytical models are developed: one predicts the accuracy impact of a given reuse pattern (approximate computation), and one predicts latency on the target microcontroller. These models enable efficient search over the generalized reuse space to select patterns that best trade off accuracy and speed for a given DNN and hardware.

title: Introducing Instruction-Accurate Simulators for Performance Estimation of Autotuning Workloads
problem: Autotuning ML workloads typically requires execution on target hardware to evaluate implementation variants, but target hardware availability is limited. Scalability is constrained by hardware access when exploring large optimization spaces.
method: Framework enables autotuning workload execution on instruction-accurate simulators (not target hardware). Machine learning predictors trained on simulation statistics forecast performance on target hardware. Evaluated on x86, ARM, and RISC-V simulators; predictors consistently identify the best implementation in top 3% of predictions.

title: Micro-MAMA: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Multicore Prefetching
problem: Independent RL-based prefetchers on each core of a multicore system compete for shared memory bandwidth without coordination, causing each agent to greedily claim excessive bandwidth and converging to sub-optimal system-wide policies. This problem is an instance of the multi-agent credit assignment and non-stationarity challenge in MARL.
method: MAMA uses a two-tier architecture: distributed local multi-armed bandit agents on each core narrow the joint-action search space by selecting among local prefetch aggressiveness options, while a central supervisor agent with global bandwidth visibility learns joint policies that maximize system-wide throughput or fairness. Key local agents receive system-level perspective signals (estimated global bandwidth usage) to discourage actions that harm other cores. The supervisor uses a lightweight bandit over the local agents' reduced action space, avoiding the exponential joint-action blow-up of fully centralized control.

title: Qtenon: Towards Low-Latency Architecture Integration for Accelerating Hybrid Quantum-Classical Computing
problem: Hybrid quantum-classical algorithms are bottlenecked by the decoupled architecture of current quantum hardware systems, which lacks low-latency communication channels and fine-grained software control for tightly coordinating quantum and classical computation. The high round-trip latency between host processor and quantum accelerator prevents real-time feedback loops required by variational algorithms.
method: Qtenon is a RISC-V extended chip implemented in Chisel that tightly couples classical and quantum processing via three hardware components: a unified memory hierarchy serving as a shared communication buffer between the host and quantum accelerators, an efficient quantum controller with dedicated data paths, and a multi-stage processing pipeline that exploits instruction-level parallelism across quantum-classical interaction phases. A custom ISA extension provides instructions for data communication, computation, fine-grained synchronization, and efficient scheduling of quantum-host interaction.

title: Segmented Angular Pre-Processing for Accurate and Efficient In-Memory Vector Similarity Search
problem: Energy-efficient vector similarity search (VSS) using cosine similarity in high-dimensional spaces, particularly for few-shot learning and approximate nearest neighbor search, while reducing vector data movement.
method: Seg-Cos framework leverages both EX-TCAM and Best-TCAM for angular VSS via dedicated preprocessing and encoding: vectors are segmented and encoded as circular ranges based on angles and magnitudes; Locality-aware Compute Mapping (LCM) reduces row activations; LUT Aggregation (LAG) enables multi-precision computations by combining multiple small LUT results.

title: FPGA-TrustZone: Security Extension of TrustZone to FPGA for SoC-FPGA Heterogeneous Architecture
problem: FPGAs in heterogeneous SoC platforms lack trusted execution environment (TEE) support; existing ARM TrustZone works only on CPUs and cannot protect FPGA workloads.
method: FPGA-TrustZone extends ARM TrustZone's security model to FPGA by implementing TEE mechanisms at the SoC interconnect and FPGA fabric level, enforcing access control and isolation between trusted and untrusted FPGA code paths.

title: Simplifying and Accelerating NOR Flash I/O Stack for RAM-Restricted Microcontrollers
problem: NOR flash file systems for RAM-restricted microcontrollers migrate block-level data organization and wear leveling logic from RAM into flash, introducing fine-grained block-level management that causes frequent index updates and full-device scans. This results in severe I/O amplification that worsens when the management layers are decoupled across the I/O stack.
method: The paper redesigns the NOR flash I/O stack to eliminate the decoupled block-level management abstraction, instead employing coarse-grained, integrated data organization that reduces index update frequency. Wear leveling is restructured to operate at a coarser granularity aligned with the NOR flash erase unit, avoiding the fine-grained scanning overhead. The resulting simplified stack collapses previously separate software layers to reduce coupling and I/O amplification jointly.

title: Late Breaking Results: An Efficient and Scalable Track Assignment with GPU Parallelism
problem: Track assignment in physical design (between global and detail routing) is compute-intensive; sequential algorithms are slow and limit design closure iteration times in large-scale chip designs.
method: GPU-accelerated parallel track assignment algorithm that exploits the independence and divisibility of track assignment tasks into fine-grained parallelizable units. Employs asynchronous parallelism strategy to partition computation of routing resources and track assignment; simultaneously considers global and local nets for improved routability estimation.

title: SeaCache: Efficient and Adaptive Caching for Sparse Accelerators
problem: Sparse tensor accelerators suffer from poor on-chip SRAM utilization because variable-length sparse fibers (rows/columns of nonzero data) do not map cleanly into fixed-size cache blocks, wasting capacity. Theoretically optimal replacement policies (e.g., Belady OPT) require expensive on-chip metadata that consumes significant die area.
method: SeaCache combines three techniques targeting sparse on-demand caches integrated in domain-specific accelerators. First, fiber packing and splitting maps variable-length sparse fibers into fixed-size cache blocks with high utilization by splitting long fibers across multiple blocks and packing short fibers together. Second, a practical replacement policy approximates OPT-like behavior at low implementation cost by exploiting access-pattern regularities in sparse computations. Third, an adaptive space-sharing mechanism dynamically partitions the cache between actual data and replacement policy metadata using a two-phase approach that measures and adjusts the optimal partition ratio at runtime.

title: Me-MPK: Accelerating Krylov Subspace Solvers via Memory-efficient Matrix-Power Kernel
problem: Matrix-Power Kernels (MPK) for Krylov subspace methods rely on repeated SpMVs with the same matrix but suffer from data dependencies that block cache reuse and symmetric SpMVs incur data conflicts during shared-memory parallelization, limiting speedup on multi-core CPUs.
method: Me-MPK constructs a unified dependency graph for sparse matrices capturing all potential dependencies and conflicts; performs architecture-aware recursive partitioning into independent subgraphs with a separating subgraph that decouples conflicts; schedules subgraphs for parallel SpMV/symmetric-SpMV execution in order to maximize cache reuse while eliminating synchronization overhead.

title: Security Opportunities and Challenges for Disaggregated Architectures (Invited)
problem: Disaggregated computer architectures separate CPU, memory, storage, and networking into independently managed units communicating over networks, introducing new security attack surfaces and isolation risks.
method: Invited position paper analyzing security aspects of disaggregation across three domains: network fabric (enterprise routing), O-RAN (software-defined radio), and trusted execution environments. Discusses attack surfaces, data exposure, provenance tracking, isolation, and API security.

title: LLMs: A Driving Force in Next Generation Digital Design Automation
problem: Silicon design automation faces growing complexity and scale; current approaches lack effective methods to leverage generative AI for automating diverse design tasks.
method: A position/review paper examining the transformative potential of LLMs in silicon design automation. The work reviews current LLM applications, analyzes their readiness to support various design automation tasks, and proposes future research directions.

title: Late Breaking Results: Multi-Objective Multi-Bit Flip-Flop Placement Considering Pre-Placed Cells
problem: Clustering single-bit flip-flops into multi-bit flip-flops reduces power and area but causes excessive displacement during legalization that degrades timing, especially with pre-placed cells in the design.
method: Employs a force model to relocate flip-flops and reduce timing violations, integrates clustering and legalization to minimize displacement-induced timing degradation, and uses a multi-objective function to select flip-flop candidates suitable for MBFF clustering while optimizing timing, power, area, and bin utilization.

title: Push Multicast: A Speculative and Coherent Interconnect for Mitigating Manycore CPU Communication Bottleneck
problem: In manycore processors running parallel workloads, multiple cores repeatedly fetch the same shared cacheline at different times, consuming redundant LLC and NoC bandwidth through independent demand requests. The reactive cache hierarchy does not exploit temporal redundancy in same-data accesses across cores.
method: Push Multicast transforms the LLC into a proactive agent: when it services a demand request, it simultaneously pushes the data to other predicted sharers via multicast, amortizing the bandwidth cost of same-data deliveries. A coherent in-network filter is installed in routers to prune outstanding demand requests that match an in-flight push, preventing redundant traffic. A dynamic pause/resume mechanism adaptively disables pushing when contention is detected, avoiding interference between push-traffic and normal demand traffic.
